newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bank stocks active on speculative interest.
newsitem.headline: French bank stocks active on speculative interest.

text.p: Shares in Credit Commercial de France (CCF) and other French banks rose on the Paris bourse on Monday on speculative interest stirred by an article in the Financial Times about a French banking sector study.
CCF shares were 3.5 percent higher at 265.80 francs at 1305 GMT while the bourse's CAC-40 index was up 0.44 percent.

In its weekend edition, the FT cited a Eurostaf study which considers Credit National and CCF as potential takeover targets. Credit National shares slightly outperformed the market, gaining 0.64 percent at 361.30 francs.

Eurostaf considers that Societe Marseillaise de Credit and some of the CIC group's regional banks could be sold to foreign banks and Banque Hervet could be acquired by a French institution. CIC's shares were up 2.10 percent at 340 francs.
According to the article, Eurostaf does not see megamergers among large French banks. It expects Credit Lyonnais may end up under foreign control after its restructuring.
